news_codex_ratings.json.review_mode: Scheduled cloud dual-review; independent Codex desk
limitations: Confidence values are subjective evidence confidence, not return probabilities. News remains unweighted in the trading score.

Only material new or materially changed evidence is reviewed in this run. Valid current-session ratings from prior Codex reviews are carried forward when no contrary evidence has appeared; an unreviewed story is not a Neutral rating.
Stories not reviewed are not Neutral ratings.

reviewed_stories.title: Fertilizer offtake falls 15% YoY in August 2026
reviewed_stories.linkage_detail: Sector demand evidence for tracked fertilizer producers FFC and EFERT. Lower domestic offtake is a direct sector-volume headwind, but the article does not provide company-level sales splits.
reviewed_stories.reason: NFDC data reported total nutrient offtake down 15.2% YoY in August, with urea down 14.2% and DAP down 7.9%. The broader Kharif picture is less severe: total nutrient offtake is down 3.7%, cumulative urea is up 2.9%, while DAP is down 24.5%. This is negative sector demand evidence, but not enough to infer the same earnings impact for FFC and EFERT.

OGDC.reason: Hormuz traffic remains severely constrained, but Brent fell to $101.71 as diplomacy hopes and recovering Saudi shipments reduced the risk premium. The upstream effect remains positive.
OGDC.relevance: Sector link: Oil & Gas Exploration; OGDC directly sells produced hydrocarbons.

PPL.reason: Hormuz traffic remains severely constrained, but Brent fell to $101.71 as diplomacy hopes and recovering Saudi shipments reduced the risk premium. The upstream effect remains positive.
PPL.relevance: Sector link: Oil & Gas Exploration; PPL directly produces and sells hydrocarbons.

MARI.reason: Hormuz disruption remains supportive for upstream hydrocarbons, while Brent's fall to $101.71 and recovering Saudi flows reduce the supply-risk premium. MARI remains positive at lower confidence because crude is only part of its hydrocarbon exposure.
MARI.relevance: Sector link: Oil & Gas Exploration; MARI produces and sells hydrocarbons.

FCEPL.reason: CEO and director Kashan Hasan has resigned but remains through his notice period, and no successor, earnings, cash-flow or strategic change is disclosed. The direct governance event is therefore neutral on current evidence.
FCEPL.relevance: Direct link: FrieslandCampina Engro Pakistan Limited (FCEPL).

Oil Marketing.reason: Government says fuel supply is being maintained and relief payments reached about 7,300 pumps, but the fresh article does not establish settlement of OMC price-differential claims or implementation of the pending margin increase.
Oil Marketing.relevance: Sector link: Oil Marketing, including PSO.

Gas Distribution.reason: Another long-term Qatari LNG cargo has safely crossed Hormuz and is expected at Pakistan's import facility by Tuesday, reducing immediate shortage and expensive spot-purchase risk. Distributor-specific throughput, tariff and receivable effects are not disclosed.
Gas Distribution.relevance: Sector link: Gas Distribution, including SNGP and SSGC; operating-supply context rather than company-specific earnings evidence.

Power Generation.reason: August national power generation rose 5.1% YoY, but the fuel mix shifted sharply and average generation cost rose 38% YoY. Aggregate generation does not establish tracked-company dispatch, tariff, receivable or earnings changes.
Power Generation.relevance: Sector link: Power Generation, including HUBC and KEL. Not direct evidence for POWER, which is Power Cement Limited.

Fertilizer.reason: August fertilizer demand weakened materially: total nutrient offtake fell 15.2% YoY, urea fell 14.2% and DAP fell 7.9%. Kharif cumulative data are less severe overall, with urea up 2.9% but DAP down 24.5%, so the sector headwind is real but not uniform across products or companies.
Fertilizer.relevance: Sector link: Fertilizer, including tracked FFC and EFERT. The article gives sector volumes, not company-level sales splits.
